prize_parts.citation: for developing empirical methods to estimate demand and competition in differentiated-product markets and dynamic industries

statement.case_for: I keep B047 as my preferred single-achievement prize. The Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes random-coefficients demand framework, with endogenous prices and product-level data, is a compact, well-defined discovery with a clean three-name attribution: Berry (1994) and BLP (1995) on demand, and Pakes' separate dynamic-industry and estimation work. It is also a mature contribution. Three decades of use in merger review, antitrust, regulation, auctions, trade and health show that it is a method and not merely a model. As a market-design theorist I value work that connects formal structure to measured, policy-relevant outcomes, and this work does that. Industrial organisation has not been recognised recently, and I apply the same standards of attribution, maturity and demonstrated influence that I apply to every other shortlisted field.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that the credit cap of three leaves out Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin, whose contributions to empirical industrial organisation and dynamic-industry estimation are real. Structural estimation also rests on functional-form and equilibrium assumptions, so some of the headline results (markups, merger effects) are model-dependent. There is a competing case for B006, where the theory is foundational and the post-2008 record is strong, and for B023, where the policy influence is large. I judge B047 slightly ahead on attribution clarity, maturity and breadth of use, but this is a close call, and my knowledge rests on background knowledge and not on verified citation data.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranks B047 first. She sees BLP as a clear, compact core of three with Pakes' Ericson-Pakes work as an additional foundation, and she asks whether the Committee would also want to honour the Bresnahan/Reiss tradition or the dynamic-games work.
responses.response: I agree that BLP is a clean core and that Pakes' dynamic-industry work adds to his share. I would qualify her open question, though. The Bresnahan-Reiss entry and market-structure work is a distinct achievement and not an extension of BLP, so folding it in would dilute attribution. Adding it as a second part would also require a larger set of people than the three-name limit allows without removing someone from the BLP trio. I would therefore treat the omission of Bresnahan and Reiss as a real cost of the cap, not as something to be resolved by enlarging this prize.

responses.point: Hassler ranks B006 first but proposes only Kiyotaki and Moore. He argues that Gertler's accelerator work builds on Bernanke-Gertler, which Bernanke's 2022 prize partly recognised, so a two-person award is the cleanest attribution, although the 2022 overlap could count against it.
responses.response: I find his attribution argument persuasive. It addresses the weakest point in the three-name version of B006 that I ranked third, namely Gertler's credit sharing with an existing laureate, and it makes B006 a stronger alternative than I assumed in my opening. It does not remove my concern about thematic proximity to the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises, or about the contested empirical identification of collateral channels. For those reasons I keep B047 ahead, but B006 with Kiyotaki and Moore is the alternative I would most readily support.

responses.point: Strömberg ranks B047 first and B023 third. He proposes only Autor and Hanson for B023 as the tightest attribution, noting that Katz shares credit on skill-biased change with Acemoglu, Goldin and Murphy, and that Dorn and Katz are therefore omitted.
responses.response: His argument pushes me to reconsider my own B023 trio. My opening included Katz, but the China-shock work belongs to Autor, Dorn and Hanson, while Katz's contribution is the earlier skill-biased technical change and wage-structure strand. Treating these as one discovery blurs attribution, and a two-name Autor-Hanson award would exclude Dorn, a real co-originator. This lowers my confidence in B023 as a single coherent prize and is one reason I keep it only as an alternative. I agree with his and Hjalmarsson's assessment that BLP's attribution is considerably cleaner.

responses.point: Krusell ranks B006 first and B047 second. He stresses the durability of the collateral-constraint and financial-accelerator tradition, its vindication after 2008, and the uncertainty over whether the credit should go to Gertler or to the Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist line.
responses.response: I agree that B006 is mature and foundational, and that the 2008 crisis tested its predictions. Our difference is mostly on attribution and novelty. The B006 credit has to be drawn around Bernanke's earlier recognition and the 2022 prize, and we disagree on how heavily to weight that. I do not treat the number of first-place votes as evidence of scientific merit, and I regard the choice between B006 and B047 as a legitimate difference in judgement.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee would accept the exclusion of Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin under the three-name cap, or would regard the omission as a defect.
How model-dependent the headline structural-IO results are, given reliance on functional-form and equilibrium assumptions.
Whether the 2022 prize and Bernanke's earlier recognition reduce the marginal case for B006 enough to leave B047 clearly ahead.
My assessments rely on general background knowledge and not on independently verified citation or influence data.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile for B047 or its credited names. My profile lists no co-authorship or institutional tie to Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes or the other B047 names, nor to the alternatives B006 and B023. I note only that I am an SSE affiliate alongside committee members Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg, which is a collegial affiliation and not a candidate-related connection.
